svg.title: Believe the works
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 5 panels. Panel 1 (John 10:22-30): Jesus walks in Solomon's colonnade on a grey winter day; the authorities gather around Him. Caption: "Jerusalem, in winter, at the Feast of Dedication. Jesus is walking in the temple, in the colonnade of Solomon." An authority says: "If you are the Christ, tell us plainly." Jesus says: "I and the Father are one." Panel 2 (John 10:31-33): the authorities take up stones. An authority says: "You, a man, make yourself God! Stone him!" Panel 3 (John 10:37-38): Jesus answers, arms open. Jesus says: "The Father is in me and I am in the Father. Do not take my word for it: believe the works." Panel 4 (John 9:7, 25-34), a flashback: outside the synagogue the healed man, hands raised, faces the authorities. Caption: "Earlier: Jesus gave sight to a man born blind. The authorities questioned the man." The healed man says: "Though I was blind, now I see! If this man were not from God, he could do nothing." An authority says: "Would you teach us? Out!" Panel 5 (John 10:34-35; Psalm 82:6-7): Jesus faces the authorities, their stones still in their hands. Jesus says: "God gave you His word and called you ‘gods’. But your works lead to death." The point: Jesus’ works are the Father's own. They show that the Father is in Him and He is in the Father, so you can believe the works and believe Him (John 10:38).
